openings.claim: A removable strip bridge with opposed contact stops may retain both plates and permit gloved service from unmarked regions. Replace friction-preload dependence with translation boundaries and a releasable lift restraint: drill, optionally plier-bend, and bolt strips through existing slots; cushion contacts with cork.
openings.discriminator: Nearest rival: incumbent cork friction clamp. If compliant geometry exists, stops should hold both plates within 1 mm despite magnetic releases of 7 N versus spare 3 N. Repeatable boundary arrest contrasts with possible progressive friction slip under insufficient preload; neither behavior is established. Awkward screwdriver access could defeat sixty-second service. Untested rival prevents superiority claims.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, use ruler and loose supplied parts to check slot fit, support, stop spacing allowing less than 1 mm motion, bridge access, and gloved extraction without edge contact; reject if these cannot coexist. Fabricate one arrangement within eighty minutes using at most four strips, six bolts with nuts, and four cork pads; drill strips only. Within twenty observation minutes, conduct three twenty-manual-stroke runs: original, spare, final spare. Measure displacement against carriage marks; inspect stop contact/deformation. Perform three timed removal/return checks; final spare removal wears thick gloves. Release bridge with supplied screwdriver; handle unmarked regions only.
openings.uncertainty: Unresolved: M4 slot compatibility and anchoring without rail detachment; strip dimensions, stiffness and plier bendability; support, glove access, extraction and repeatable reseating. Geometry and stroke forces remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves contact-boundary mechanism, friction rival, conditional predictions, service challenge, bounded probe and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Proceed only after geometry checks. Keep marked 30 mm edge exposed, additions outside stroke clearance, carriage attached to rails; never drill, cut, heat or glue plate/carriage. Defeat: displacement above 1 mm, service above sixty seconds, deformation, edge contact, clearance intrusion or resource/time overrun. Supplied synthetic task; bounded probe, not deployment.
